sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Block a user handler
sections.what: Blocks another user for the signed-in fan after checking the body, and returns an empty success response.
sections.why: Likely reason: blocking is done through the moderation service so the rules stay in one place. The shared schema is reused with a different name here.
sections.watch_out: The schema is named transferInput, which is also used for handing over a crew, so editing it affects both features.

summary: Lets a signed-in fan block another user. The request body must contain that user's id.
purpose: Lets fans stop seeing and interacting with someone they do not want to deal with.
why: Blocking is a safety feature, and the route only passes the request on to the service.
how: 1) Confirms the user is signed in. 2) Checks the body contains a user id in the expected shape. 3) Calls the block service. 4) Returns an empty success response.
inputs: A POST request with a JSON body holding a user id. The signed-in user comes from the session.
outputs: An empty 204 response when the block succeeds.
risks: The body check uses a schema named for ownership transfer, so changing that schema changes this route too.
debug: If blocking fails, check the body shape and the block function in the moderation service.
